newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-DOURTHE KICKS DAX INTO QUARTER-FINALS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-DOURTHE KICKS DAX INTO QUARTER-FINALS.

text.p: French international Richard Dourthe kicked Dax into the European Cup quarter-finals on Saturday with 17 points in his side's 22-18 win over Pontypridd.
Dax took the early lead when winger Hugo Mola hacked through to score the only try of the match.
The match then degenerated into a penalty exchange between Dourthe and Pontypridd fly-half Neil Jenkins with the French side finishing as narrow winners.
Defending champions Toulouse recovered handsomely from last week's thrashing by Wasps to crush Northern Ireland side Munster 60-19 on Saturday and clinch a place in the knockout stages.

Toulouse joined Cardiff as qualifiers from pool D while English champions Bath made sure of progressing from pool A as fly-half Mike Catt scored 33 points, one short of the competition record, in their 50-27 away win over Treviso of Italy.
Also through to the next round were Harlequins, who beat Caledonia 56-35 in pool C, while Llanelli of Wales qualified despite losing 25-16 to pool B winners Leicester.

Leinster of Ireland finished level on points with Llanelli after a penalty two minutes from the end gave them a dramatic 25-23 win over Pau of France but Llanelli go through because of a superior points difference.
Three clubs, Brive of France, Leicester of England and Cardiff of Wales, had already ensured quarter-final places.
Toulouse struggled in the first half against Munster and led only 17-9 before turning on the pressure in the final 40 minutes.

The champions, hammered 77-17 by Wasps last weekend, went on a try-scoring spree after the interval. Michel Marfaing scored three, Emile Ntamack and Christian Califano two apiece while David Berty and Stephane Ougier scored one each.
Catt, bidding for a place in England's international against Italy later this month, scored four tries, five conversions and a penalty for Bath.

His first try stemmed from a break from half-way after 12 minutes, a chip ahead and some deft handling as Bath took a 28-8 halftime lead and then in five magic minutes after the interval Catt added three more.
With Bath leading 47-8, a really big score looked likely but the Italians fought back with a burst of 19 points without reply until Catt added a final penalty for the English champions.

Leinster's dramatic, but in the end fruitless, win over Pau at Donneybrook owed much to the boot of fly-half Alan McGowan who was successful with seven of his nine kicks and landed the winning penalty in the 78th minute from nearly 10 metres inside the Pau half of the field.
Wasps, although with no chance of qualifying for the next stage, continued their recovery with a 33-23 away win over Italian champions Milan who finished pointless and bottom of pool D.
